matchstick.title: Compute numeric discrepancy
matchstick.principle: Convert each Roman numeral in the equation to its integer value, sum the terms on each side, and calculate the difference between the left‑hand side and the right‑hand side.
matchstick.when_to_apply: At the start of solving a matchstick puzzle, before considering any stick moves.
matchstick.example: For 'XII = XIII + IV', the left side is 12 and the right side is 17, giving a discrepancy of –5.

matchstick.title: Enumerate single‑stick numeral transformations
matchstick.principle: List all Roman‑numeral characters that can be obtained by adding or removing a single matchstick from each numeral present, while keeping the remaining sticks in a valid shape.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After computing the discrepancy, generate the set of possible value changes for each character.
matchstick.example: From X you can obtain V by moving one diagonal; from I you can obtain II by adding a vertical stick.

matchstick.title: Validate source and destination characters
matchstick.principle: After moving a stick, ensure that the character you removed it from still forms a valid Roman numeral or operator, and that the character you added it to also becomes a valid symbol.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Immediately after proposing a stick relocation, before arithmetic check.
matchstick.example: Removing a diagonal from X leaves V, which is valid; adding that diagonal to the same X to form V is allowed.

matchstick.title: V↔X transformation (reposition diagonal)
matchstick.principle: A diagonal stick can be moved from a V to make an X (value +5) or removed from an X to make a V (value –5), preserving stick orientation.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the numeric discrepancy is a multiple of 5 or when a V or X appears in the equation.
matchstick.example: Changing the X in XIII to V reduces its value by 5, turning XIII into VIII.

matchstick.title: I↔II vertical addition/removal
matchstick.principle: Adding a vertical stick to an I creates II (value +1); removing a vertical stick from II yields I (value –1).
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the discrepancy is ±1 and an I or II is present.
matchstick.example: Changing I to II increases the total by 1.

matchstick.title: Operator change – to + (or + to –)
matchstick.principle: A plus sign consists of a vertical and a horizontal stick; removing the vertical turns it into a minus sign, and adding a vertical to a minus sign creates a plus sign, changing the sign of the adjacent term.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the discrepancy equals twice the value of the term after the operator, or when a sign flip can resolve the equation.
matchstick.example: Changing '+' to '-' in 'X = X + I' makes the equation 'X = X - I', adjusting the RHS by –2.

matchstick.title: Respect stick orientation
matchstick.principle: Sticks keep their original orientation; a diagonal stick cannot be used as a vertical or horizontal stick, and vice versa.
matchstick.when_to_apply: During any stick relocation, ensure the moved stick is placed with the same orientation it had originally.
matchstick.example: A diagonal from X cannot be placed to form an I.

matchstick.title: Re‑evaluate arithmetic after each move
matchstick.principle: After applying a candidate stick relocation, recompute the integer values of the whole equation to verify that the equality holds.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After any proposed transformation, before finalizing the answer.
matchstick.example: After turning X into V, recalculate the RHS to confirm it now equals the LHS.

matchstick.title: Match discrepancy with possible value changes
matchstick.principle: Prioritize single‑stick transformations whose numeric effect (increase or decrease) matches the computed discrepancy, using known value changes of numeral and operator modifications.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the discrepancy is known, filter the list of possible transformations to those that adjust the total by exactly that amount.
matchstick.example: With a discrepancy of –5, consider X→V (–5) or '+'→'–' (adjusts RHS by –2·operand).

matchstick.title: Operator stick relocation
matchstick.principle: Horizontal or vertical sticks can be moved between operators (e.g., from ‘=’ to ‘-’) or from an operator to a numeral, changing the operator type while preserving stick orientation.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the discrepancy cannot be resolved by numeral changes alone, consider altering operators by moving their sticks.
matchstick.example: Moving a horizontal stick from ‘=’ to ‘+’ can turn ‘+’ into ‘=’ and ‘=’ into ‘-’.

matchstick.description: Treating a diagonal stick as a vertical I
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model forgets that stick orientation is fixed and assumes any stick can become any other orientation.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Enforce that a stick retains its original orientation; a diagonal can only form diagonal parts of V or X, never a vertical I.

matchstick.description: Leaving an invalid source character after removal
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model checks only the destination validity, overlooking that the source must also remain a valid symbol.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: After each removal, verify that the source character still matches a valid Roman numeral or operator.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model treats operators as immutable or forgets the simple vertical‑stick change.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Include operator conversion in the list of possible single‑stick moves and evaluate its numeric impact.

matchstick.description: Skipping arithmetic verification after a visual change
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model assumes visual correctness implies arithmetic correctness.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Always recalculate the integer values after any stick move and compare both sides.

matchstick.description: Assuming the equality sign cannot be altered
matchstick.why_it_happens: Misinterpretation that the equality sign is fixed in the puzzle.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Allow the equality sign to be changed (e.g., to ‘-’ or ‘+’) by moving its horizontal sticks, provided the resulting symbols are valid.
